therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: renally-impaired heart transplant recipients on calcineurin inhibitor (CNI) therapy
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Change from baseline in calculated creatinine clearance (Cockcroft-Gault) at 52 weeks post-randomization

results.effect_size: Sirolimus +3.03 vs CNI -1.35 mL/min/1.73m² (LS mean change from baseline at Week 52)
results.target_engagement_evidence: Target trough level of 7–15 ng/mL for sirolimus monitored throughout study
biomarker_changes: Serum creatinine change at Week 52: CNI +4.76 mcmol/L vs SRL -4.39 mcmol/L (p=0.001)
MDRD-based creatinine clearance change at Week 52: CNI -0.90 vs SRL +3.26 mL/min/1.73m² (p=0.010)
Annual change in creatinine clearance (Cockcroft-Gault): CNI -0.740 vs SRL +1.571 mL/min/1.73m²/year (p=0.126)
subgroup_findings: Creatinine clearance improvement with SRL vs CNI was significant at Weeks 4 (p=0.018), 16 (p<0.001), 24 (p=0.012) but not at Weeks 32 (p=0.072) or 40 (p=0.175)
21 participants in the sirolimus group required conversion back to CNI therapy
Transplant rejection SAE: 13/57 in sirolimus vs 1/57 in CNI group
Acute rejection (for cause biopsies): 5 SRL vs 1 CNI (p=0.206)
Acute rejection (standard of care biopsies): 2 SRL vs 0 CNI (p=0.476)
Protocol mandated biopsies (SRL only): 7 acute rejections detected
safety_signals: Transplant rejection SAE markedly higher in sirolimus group (13/57 vs 1/57)
21/57 sirolimus patients required conversion back to CNI
Sudden death reported in 1 sirolimus patient
Endocarditis, arrhythmia, cerebral ischemia each reported in 1 sirolimus patient

dose_info.dose: 1 mg or 2 mg tablets (sirolimus); CNI dosed to investigator-determined trough
dose_info.schedule: once daily (sirolimus); site and patient specific (CNI)
dose_info.dose_modifications: 21 sirolimus patients converted back to CNI therapy
